js.shellui.kmx-chu-ban.t: The chart is drawn by the Luo Shu with South at the top — the classical way, the reverse of an ordinary map. Each cell: gate (large line) · heaven-plate star and deity · heaven-plate stem (bold) over earth-plate stem (italic). #n is the relative rank among the nine palaces, not a verdict of fortune.

js.shellui.kmx-chu-bang.t: The Engine column is the good/bad verdict of the classical algorithm. The Score column is a relative rank computed by the page so that it can always point to the best direction — formula: auspicious gate +3 / inauspicious −3, star and deity ±2, Three Marvels +2, +1 per auspicious pattern and −1 per inauspicious pattern. Measured over 366 charts across a year, only 26.5% of charts have a palace the engine rates auspicious, so reading the Engine column alone, the chart says "everywhere is bad" most of the time.

luangiai.tu-vi-dau-so-la-mot.t: Zi Wei Dou Shu (Purple Star Astrology) is a traditional system of Chinese destiny reading. It casts a chart from the lunar birth hour, with 12 palaces and a system of major and minor stars. Refined over many generations, it became popular in Vietnam through the translation of Zi Wei Dou Shu Xin Bian (Tử Vi Đẩu Số Tân Biên) by Vân Đằng Thái Thứ Lang, and grew into a distinct Vietnamese school.
